newsitem.title: FRANCE: Power-sharing boosts Chirac more than Jospin-poll.
newsitem.headline: Power-sharing boosts Chirac more than Jospin-poll.

text.p: The first six weeks of enforced "cohabitation", or power-sharing, between Gaullist President Jacques Chirac and Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin have benefited the head of state more than his premier, an opinion poll showed on Sunday.

The IFOP survey for the weekly Le Journal du Dimanche said that 42 percent of those asked were happy with Chirac's performance, up four percent on the previous month. Forty-three percent, against 45 percent, were dissatisfied with him.

The poll, carried out on July 10-18 among 1,867 people, showed a weaker increase for Jospin, whose popularity went up to 48 percent from 47 percent a month earlier. But 29 percent were unhappy with him, against 20 percent in June.

The survey was carried out during a clash between Chirac and Jospin following a televised interview on July 14 in which the president fired a volley of criticism at the premier on policies ranging from privatisation to nuclear power, Europe and immigration.
Two days later, Jospin firmly reminded the head of state, shorn of much of his power by the leftist win in a parliamentary election on June 1, of his rights at a cabinet meeting.
